items.followUp: Name the two major phases of the cell cycle and state what happens in each.

rubric.why: The cell cycle is the sequence of events from one cell division to the next.
rubric.description: Defines the cell cycle as the sequence of events between successive cell divisions.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a definition that describes the events from one division to the next.

rubric.why: Interphase and the mitotic phase are the major phases of the cell cycle.
rubric.description: Names interphase and the mitotic phase (M phase).
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for naming both major phases.

modelAnswer: The cell cycle is the sequence of events from one cell division to the next.
Its major phases are interphase and the mitotic phase (M phase).

items.followUp: Differentiate between benign and malignant tumors.

rubric.why: Benign tumors are non-cancerous, usually remain localized, and do not spread to other parts of the body.
rubric.description: States that benign tumors are non-cancerous and remain localized without spreading.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing the non-spreading, localized nature of benign tumors.

rubric.why: Malignant tumors are cancerous, invade surrounding tissues, and may spread to other parts of the body by metastasis.
rubric.description: States that malignant tumors are cancerous and invade or spread.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing invasion into surrounding tissues or spread to other parts of the body.

modelAnswer: Benign tumors are non-cancerous, usually remain localized, and do not spread to other parts of the body.
Malignant tumors are cancerous; they invade surrounding tissues and may spread to other parts of the body (metastasis).

items.followUp: Differentiate between anabolic and catabolic reactions, including their energy changes.

rubric.why: Catabolism breaks complex molecules into simpler molecules and releases energy.
rubric.description: Defines catabolism as the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler ones.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the breakdown direction of catabolism.

rubric.why: Anabolism synthesizes complex molecules from simpler molecules and requires energy.
rubric.description: Defines anabolism as the synthesis of complex molecules from simpler ones.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating the synthesis direction of anabolism.

modelAnswer: Catabolism is the breakdown of complex molecules into simpler molecules, releasing energy.
Anabolism is the synthesis of complex molecules from simpler molecules, requiring energy.
